object.title: NP-completeness conjecture for metric divisorial gonality
object.statement: Fix a positive integer $r$. For a metric graph $\Gamma=(G,l)$ with rational edge lengths, the $r^{th}$ Metric Divisorial Gonality problem asks whether $\operatorname{dgon}_r(\Gamma)\leq k$ for a given integer $k$. **Metric divisorial gonality conjecture.** The $r^{th}$ Metric Divisorial Gonality problem is NP-complete. Membership in NP is known when both $r$ and $k$ are fixed; extending the argument to variable $k$, for example with $k$ bounded by $r|V(G)|$, is left open.
object.source_name: Ralph Morrison and Lucas Tolley, “Computing higher graph gonality is hard”, arXiv:2208.03573 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03573

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

object.title: Rota–Mason conjectures on unimodality and log-concavity of Whitney numbers
object.statement:
Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a loopless matroid of rank $k$ and cardinality $n$, and let $W_i$ be the number of flats of rank $i$. **Whitney-number coefficient conjectures.** The sequence $W_0,\ldots,W_k$ is unimodal, the sequence $W_0,\ldots,W_k$ is log-concave with $W_i^2\geq W_{i-1}W_{i+1}$ for $1\leq i\leq k-1$, and the normalized sequence $W_0/\binom n0,\ldots,W_k/\binom nk$ is log-concave, equivalently

$$
W_i^2\geq\frac{i+1}{i}\frac{n-i+1}{n-i}W_{i-1}W_{i+1}\qquad(1\leq i\leq k-1).
$$

These are the classical coefficient conjectures for the $\mathrm{W}$-polynomial, attributed in the paper to Rota and Mason. The source says that the unimodality conjecture remains open; no resolution status is supplied for the full combined list.
object.source_name: Luis Ferroni and Benjamin Schröter, “Valuative invariants for large classes of matroids”, arXiv:2208.04893 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04893

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

object.title: The word-map nonconstancy conjecture for simple compact Lie groups
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected simple compact Lie group with trivial center. A **non-constant word** is an element of $G\ast F_d$ that does not lie in $G$ itself; its evaluation on $G^d$ is the associated word map.

**Word-map nonconstancy conjecture.** Every non-constant word defines a non-constant word map.

The trivial-center hypothesis is necessary, since a nontrivial central element produces a non-constant word with constant evaluation. The claim also fails for certain semisimple, non-simple compact groups, while the conjecture asks for the corresponding nonconstancy property in the simple case.
object.source_name: Michael Larsen and Aner Shalev, “Identities with coefficients in simple compact Lie groups”, arXiv:2208.07418 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07418

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

object.title: Coloring probability inequality for minimal elements of posets
object.statement:
Let $P$ be a connected $n$-element poset with minimal elements $m_1,\ldots,m_s$. Define a coloring $c:P\to\mathcal{P}([s])$ by putting $i\in c(x)$ if $x\geq_P m_i$, where $[s]=\{1,\ldots,s\}$. Let $L_{n-2}$ denote the labeling obtained after $n-2$ applications of promotion, and let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the relevant probability distribution on labelings.

**Coloring probability conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{P}\left(c(L_{n-2}^{-1}(1))=\{s\}\,\middle|\,L(m_{s-1})=n\right)\geq\mathbb{P}\left(c(L_{n-2}^{-1}(1))=\{s\}\,\middle|\,L(m_s)=n\right).
$$

The paper states that this inequality would imply the general bound for tangled labelings by showing that the number of tangled labelings increases when $m_{s-1}\lessdot m_s$; it remains open.
object.source_name: Eliot Hodges, “On Promotion and Quasi-tangled Labelings of Posets”, arXiv:2208.08665 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08665

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2022). “Finally, in , we present several open problems and further directions of inquiry.”

object.title: The disconnected contact-poset conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a disconnected poset. A poset is **Frobenius** when its associated type-A Lie poset algebra has index zero, and it is **toral** when it has the toral construction form described in the paper. The disjoint sum of two posets is their union with no comparabilities between the two components.

**Disconnected contact-poset conjecture.** $\mathcal{P}$ is contact if and only if it is a disjoint sum of two Frobenius, toral posets.

The paper explains that this conjecture would follow from the toral-poset conjecture for Frobenius posets, together with known results on disconnected contact type-A Lie poset algebras. The source gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Nicholas W. Mayers and Nicholas Russoniello, “On toral posets and contact Lie algebras”, arXiv:2208.09060 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.09060

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

object.title: The connected contact-poset torality conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a connected poset, and let $\mathfrak{g}_A(\mathcal{P})$ be its associated type-A Lie poset algebra. The algebra is **contact** when it has index one and admits a contact form.

**Connected contact-poset torality conjecture.** If $\mathfrak{g}_A(\mathcal{P})$ is contact, then $\mathcal{P}$ is toral.

This conjecture proposes that the toral construction captures every connected contact type-A Lie poset algebra. The source gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Nicholas W. Mayers and Nicholas Russoniello, “On toral posets and contact Lie algebras”, arXiv:2208.09060 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.09060

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

object.title: Thomas–Williams' rowmotion order conjecture for rational Tamari lattices
object.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be relatively prime positive integers. Let $\operatorname{Tam}(a,b)$ be the rational Tamari lattice of lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(a,b)$ lying strictly above $y=(b/a)x$ except at their endpoints, and let $\operatorname{Row}$ denote its rowmotion operator.

**Thomas–Williams' conjecture.** The operator

$$
\operatorname{Row}\colon\operatorname{Tam}(a,b)\to\operatorname{Tam}(a,b)
$$

has order $a+b-1$.

This conjecture gives the period of rowmotion on every rational Tamari lattice. The paper proves it for the subfamily of $m$-Tamari lattices, while the general case remains open.
object.source_name: Colin Defant and James Lin, “Rowmotion on m-Tamari and BiCambrian Lattices”, arXiv:2208.10464 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.10464

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

object.title: Periodicity conjecture for the Nabla-triangle
object.statement:
Let $p\geq2$ be an integer, and let $P=\nabla(p)$, where

$$
\nabla(p)=\{(i,k)\in[p]\times[p]\mid i+k<p+1\}.
$$

Use the same notation as for the Delta-triangle: $f$ is a $[?]$-labeling of $\widehat{P}$, $R$ is birational rowmotion, and $a=f(0)$ and $b=f(1)$. **Periodicity conjecture for the Nabla-triangle.** The Delta-triangle periodicity statement should also hold when $P=\nabla(p)$ instead of $P=\Delta(p)$. Thus, with the corresponding transpose involution $x\mapsto x'$, one should have

$$
(R^pf)(x)=a\overline{b}\cdot f(x')\cdot\overline{a}b.
$$

If true, this would generalize the cited commutative result; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
object.source_name: Darij Grinberg and Tom Roby, “Birational rowmotion on a rectangle over a noncommutative ring”, arXiv:2208.11156 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.11156

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

object.title: Smith normal form conjecture for the walk matrix of the extended Dynkin graph
object.statement:
Let $\tilde{D}_n$ be the extended Dynkin graph with $n+1$ vertices, let $W(\tilde{D}_n)$ be its walk matrix, and set

$$
r=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Smith normal form conjecture.** The Smith normal form of $W(\tilde{D}_n)$ is

$$
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{diag}(\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{r-1},n-1,0,\ldots,0), & \text{if $n$ is even},\\
\operatorname{diag}\left(\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{r-1},\frac{n-1}{2},0,\ldots,0\right), & \text{if $n$ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture gives the remaining Smith normal form data after the paper determines the rank of the walk matrix, and its verification would complete the proposed next step for the extended Dynkin graphs $\tilde{D}_n$.
object.source_name: Sunyo Moon and Seungkook Park, “The rank of the walk matrix of the extended Dynkin graph D_n”, arXiv:2208.12447 (2022).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1602.00166](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.00166).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.12447

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2022).

object.title: Madani–Kiani's generalized regularity bound for connected graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on vertex set $[n]$, let $K_m$ be the complete graph on $[m]$, let $J_{K_m,G}$ be the generalized binomial edge ideal, let $c(G)$ be the number of maximal cliques of $G$, and assume $m<n$. **Madani–Kiani's connected-graph conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{reg}(S/J_{K_m,G})\leq \min\{(m-1)c(G),n-1\}.
$$

The source says that this bound was proved for chordal graphs, but does not provide a general proof or disproof for connected graphs.
object.source_name: Priya Das, “Recent results on homological properties of binomial edge ideal of graphs”, arXiv:2209.01201 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01201

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2022). “The conjecture in general remains as one of the important open problem in this area.”

object.title: Propp's benzel tiling enumeration conjecture
object.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be integers with $2\leq a\leq b\leq 2a$ and $a+b\equiv 2\pmod 3$. Let $n$ and $k$ be the integers such that

$$
(a,b)=(n+3k,2n+3k-1).
$$

**Propp's conjecture.** The $(a,b)$-benzel has

$$
\prod_{i=1}^k \frac{(2i)!(2i+2n-2)!}{(i+n-1)!(i+n+k-1)!}
$$

tilings by right stones, rising bones, and falling bones. This conjecture concerns the previously unresolved case $a+b\equiv 2\pmod 3$; the supplied paper presents it immediately before proving related enumeration results, but the provided context does not establish whether this particular conjecture is resolved.
object.source_name: Colin Defant, Rupert Li, James Propp and Benjamin Young, “Tilings of Benzels via the Abacus Bijection”, arXiv:2209.05717 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.05717

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).

object.title: Equilibrium-count conjecture for symmetric finite trails
object.statement:
Consider the Trail of Lost Pennies on the finite trail $\llbracket -j-1,k+1\rrbracket$ in its symmetric standard form. **Finite-trail equilibrium-count conjecture.** The number of time-invariant Nash equilibria equals

$$
\max\{2(j+k)-5,1\}.
$$

The formula is presented as a conjecture about the effect of reflection symmetries on the finite-trail game; no proof or resolution is supplied in the text.
object.source_name: Alan Hammond, “On the Trail of Lost Pennies: player-funded tug-of-war on the integers”, arXiv:2209.07451 (2026).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07451

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).

object.title: The KSTH conjecture on spanning-tree decompositions of complete graphs
object.statement: Let $K_{2m}$ be the complete graph on $2m$ vertices. A **vertex-split** is a decomposition of its edge set into mutually edge-disjoint spanning trees; write the resulting group as $S_{paning}(K_{2m})$. **KSTH conjecture.** Each complete graph $K_{2m}$ can be vertex-split into a group $S_{paning}(K_{2m})$ of $m$ mutually edge-disjoint spanning trees, each with $2m-1$ edges, such that every pair of distinct spanning trees $T_i,T_j\in S_{paning}(K_{2m})$ forms a vertex-coincided graph $G=T_i[\odot_{prop}]T_j$ containing a Hamilton cycle and two perfect matchings. This asserts a structured decomposition of complete graphs into spanning trees with strong pairwise connectivity properties; the source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Bing Yao, Chao Yang, Xia Liu, Fei Ma, Jing Su, Hui Sun, Xiaohui Zhang and Yarong Mu, “Strings And Colorings Of Topological Coding Towards Asymmetric Topology Cryptography”, arXiv:2209.15312 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.15312

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2022).

object.title: The minimal surjective-strategy conjecture for wreath products
object.statement: Let $G\wr H$ be a wreath product with state group $K$, and call a surjective strategy **minimal** when it has the form $\{k_i\in K\}_{i=1}^{|K|-1}$. **Minimal strategy conjecture.** Whenever $G\wr H$ has a surjective strategy, it also has a minimal surjective strategy $\{k_i\in K\}_{i=1}^{|K|-1}$. Minimal strategies would give the shortest possible guaranteed bound discussed in the source; the conjecture is based on the examples known to the authors and remains open.
object.source_name: Peter Kagey, “Spinning switches on a wreath product”, arXiv:2210.09408 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.09408

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: Graphs of free groups with cyclic edge groups
object.statement:
Let $X$ be a compact, connected, irreducible graph of graphs with circular edge spaces.

**Graphs of free groups with cyclic edge groups.** Then $\rho_+(X)\leq 0$. Furthermore, $\sigma_+(X)<0$ unless $\pi_1(X)$ has a Baumslag--Solitar subgroup.

The source expects this conjecture to be relatively easy to prove and presents it as a warm-up for more difficult examples; no proof or resolution is supplied.
object.source_name: Henry Wilton, “Rational curvature invariants for 2-complexes”, arXiv:2210.09853 (2024).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.09853

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: The non-nested and non-separated matching conjectures for ordered complete graphs
object.statement:
Let $t,n$ be positive integers and set

$$
m=(t-1)(n-1)+2n.
$$

Consider a $t$-coloring of the edges of the ordered complete graph $K_m$, whose vertices are linearly ordered. A matching is a set of pairwise vertex-disjoint edges; it is **non-nested** if no two edges are nested and **non-separated** if no two edges are separated in the vertex order. **Ordered matching conjecture.** Every such coloring contains (i) a monochromatic non-nested matching with $n$ edges, and (ii) a monochromatic non-separated matching with $n$ edges. This conjecture asks whether the Cockayne–Lorimer bound remains valid for these two ordered matching types; the source identifies this as the main open problem and notes positive answers in several special cases.
object.source_name: János Barát, András Gyárfás and Géza Tóth, “Monochromatic spanning trees and matchings in ordered complete graphs”, arXiv:2210.10135 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.10135

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: Abreu–Goedgebeur–Labbate–Mazzuoccolo isomorphic linear-forest conjecture
object.statement: Let $G$ be a cubic graph. A **linear forest** is a forest whose components are paths, and a two-colouring of $V(G)$ induces one subgraph on each colour class. **Abreu–Goedgebeur–Labbate–Mazzuoccolo's conjecture.** The vertex set of $G$ can be two-coloured so that the two colour classes induce isomorphic linear forests. The conjecture is known for large connected cubic graphs of large girth and for some specific cubic graphs, but remains open in general.
object.source_name: Gal Kronenberg, Shoham Letzter, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Liana Yepremyan, “Decomposing cubic graphs into isomorphic linear forests”, arXiv:2210.11458 (2025).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.11458

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: Golomb–Taylor conjecture on singly periodic Costas sequences
object.statement: Let a Costas sequence be a sequence whose difference triangle has no repeated entry in any row. A sequence is **singly periodical** when every circular shift of its terms is also a Costas sequence. A Welch sequence is one obtained from the Welch construction: for a prime $p$, a primitive element $\alpha\in\mathbb{F}_p$, and $c\in\mathbb{Z}$, the sequence $\alpha^{c},\alpha^{1+c},\dots,\alpha^{p-2+c}$. **Golomb–Taylor's conjecture.** A Costas sequence is singly periodical if and only if it is Welch. Only Welch sequences are currently known to be singly periodical, so the conjecture remains open.
object.source_name: Ivelisse Rubio and Jaziel Torres, “Circular Costas maps: a multidimensional analog of circular Costas sequences”, arXiv:2210.16661 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.16661

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: Directed forcing conjecture for oriented graphs
object.statement: Let $B$ be an oriented graph, let $\overline{B}$ be its underlying undirected graph obtained by forgetting edge directions, and call $B$ directed-forcing when it has the directed forcing property. **Directed forcing conjecture.** If $B$ has a homomorphism to an edge and $\overline{B}$ contains a cycle, then $B$ has the directed forcing property. The paper proves that a homomorphism to an edge and a cycle in the underlying graph are necessary conditions for directed forcing. It conjectures that these two conditions are also sufficient, leaving the characterization open.
object.source_name: Jacob Fox, Zoe Himwich, Nitya Mani and Yunkun Zhou, “A note on directed analogues of the Sidorenko and forcing conjectures”, arXiv:2210.16971 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.16971

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2022).

object.title: The pairwise-adjacent vertices-or-edges conjecture for triangle-free graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be an $coverline{K_3}$-free graph on $n$ vertices. A set of vertices or edges is **pairwise adjacent** when every two members are adjacent, where adjacency between an edge and another member has the natural incidence/endpoint interpretation used in the source.

**Pairwise-adjacent vertices-or-edges conjecture.** Every $coverline{K_3}$-free graph on $n$ vertices has a set of

$$
\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil
$$

pairwise adjacent vertices or edges.

This conjecture is presented as an obstacle to reconciling two algorithmic approaches for proving restricted forms of Hadwiger's Conjecture. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Daniel Carter, “Hadwiger's Conjecture with Certain Forbidden Induced Subgraphs”, arXiv:2211.00259 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.00259

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).
